rich_summary: Arjuna reveals to Prince Uttara that his year-long disguise as the eunuch Brihannala was a vow taken to honor his elder brother’s command and has now ended. Relieved that his suspicions were correct, Uttara eagerly offers to serve as Arjuna’s charioteer and proudly describes the war chariot and its powerful horses. Arjuna then prepares for battle: he dons warrior gear, recalls his celestial weapons, and strings the mighty Gandiva bow, whose thunderous twang shakes the earth and alerts the Kauravas that Arjuna has returned. Though frightened by the ominous sounds and supernatural signs, Uttara is reassured by Arjuna’s confident recollection of past heroic battles against gods, demons, and kings. Raising his celestial ape-banner and blowing his terrible conch, Arjuna sets out to face the Kaurava army, steadying the terrified Uttara and reminding him of his Kshatriya duty.

highlight_spans.why: Arjuna reveals the truth about his disguise and declares the completion of his vow, marking the end of concealment and the return of the warrior.
Uttara’s enthusiastic response establishes their partnership, with the prince volunteering to serve as charioteer and praising the chariot and horses.
The dramatic moment when Arjuna strings the Gandiva bow and the thunderous sound shakes the world, signaling his presence to allies and enemies alike.
Uttara’s fear contrasts with Arjuna’s calm confidence, emphasizing the psychological tension before battle.
Arjuna recounts his past battles against celestial beings and mighty foes, reinforcing his legendary status and reassuring Uttara.

top_scenes.scene_text: Arjuna standing on the chariot beneath the Sami tree, tying back his hair and summoning his celestial weapons as they appear before him in reverence.
Arjuna strings the Gandiva bow and releases its thunderous twang while meteors fall, winds roar, and the sky darkens around the battlefield.
The chariot bearing Arjuna’s golden ape-banner descends with divine brilliance as the terrified prince Uttara watches in awe.
